patterns: how do I apply for admission
how to enroll in the college
responses: Admissions open every year in June. You need to fill the online application form, upload your documents, and appear for the entrance test or merit-based shortlisting.
To apply, visit the admissions portal, complete the form, pay the application fee, and submit required documents (marksheets, ID proof, photo).
Eligibility generally requires 10+2 with at least 60% marks in Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics for engineering courses. Check the specific course page for exact criteria.

patterns: what programs does the college offer
responses: We offer courses including Computer Science, Electronics, Mechanical, Civil Engineering, Business Administration, and Commerce. Which one are you interested in?

patterns: how many years is the degree
responses: Most undergraduate courses are 4 years long (8 semesters), while postgraduate courses are typically 2 years.

patterns: how much is the course fee
responses: The annual fee varies by course, generally between ₹80,000 to ₹1,50,000 per year, including tuition and lab charges. Check the official fee structure page for exact amounts by course.
Fees can be paid online via the student portal using net banking, UPI, or card. You can also pay offline at the accounts office. Check the academic calendar for payment deadlines.
Yes, merit-based and need-based scholarships are available. You can apply through the scholarship portal after admission confirmation, usually within the first semester.
The college has tie-ups with companies for summer and semester internships. The Training & Placement Cell shares openings and helps with applications, usually starting from the 3rd year.
Generally students with a minimum CGPA of 6.0 and no active backlogs are eligible to apply for internships through the college placement cell.
The college has a strong placement record with companies like TCS, Infosys, Wipro, and Amazon visiting campus. The average package is around ₹5-6 LPA, with the highest going up to ₹20+ LPA.
The placement process usually includes an aptitude test, technical round, group discussion, and HR interview. The Placement Cell coordinates all rounds with visiting companies.
